# cgroup_mode workload impact

- Run: `20261024T000600Z`
- Node: `k8labs-md-custom-hbsml-qx6v4-mch2q` kernel `7.3.0-k8labs`
- CPUs: 2, repetitions: 3, measurement window: 8.0 s, warmup: 2.0 s
- Mode before/after: `concur` / `concur`

## Mode semantics

| mode | model |
|---|---|
| `up` | full group weight on every CPU (F_g_n = 1) |
| `smp` | group weight distributed across the CPUs its tasks use |
| `concur` | min(tasks, cpus) x weight (per active CPU) |
| `max` | cpus x weight, clipped at nice -20 |
| `tasks` | tasks x weight (weight per runnable task) |

## Findings

- `weighted_threads`: the 4-thread/weight-100 group reaches 35.9% under `tasks`; the 1-thread/weight-400 group reaches 41.6% under the same mode.
- `weighted_threads`: `up` gives the 4-thread group 1.26x its smp CPU share.
- `weighted_threads`: `smp` gives the 4-thread group 1.00x its smp CPU share.
- `weighted_threads`: `concur` gives the 4-thread group 1.53x its smp CPU share.
- `weighted_threads`: `max` gives the 4-thread group 1.01x its smp CPU share.
- `weighted_threads`: `tasks` gives the 4-thread group 2.16x its smp CPU share.
- `weighted_threads`: the 4-thread group gains 1.53x under `concur` and 2.16x under `tasks`, but the 2-thread group does not (0.77x and 0.68x). The 2-thread group has one runnable thread per CPU, so the kernel's group runnable average does not scale it the way the simple `min(threads, cpus)` model predicts.
- `qos_nested`: `up` gives Burstable 3.01x the Guaranteed CPU share.
- `qos_nested`: `smp` gives Burstable 1.07x the Guaranteed CPU share.
- `qos_nested`: `concur` gives Burstable 2.00x the Guaranteed CPU share.
- `qos_nested`: `max` gives Burstable 1.07x the Guaranteed CPU share.
- `qos_nested`: `tasks` gives Burstable 3.98x the Guaranteed CPU share.
- `qos_nested`: `up` is not a neutral baseline on this 2-CPU worker. The 4-thread Burstable parent keeps its full weight on both CPUs while the 1-thread Guaranteed parent keeps it on one, so the measured ratio is 3.01x; `smp` stays at 1.07x and `max` at 1.07x.
- `qos_nested`: the two equal Burstable pods split 61.2% / 38.8% under `up` (across-repetition sd 9.7 points); the other modes stay within 0.2 points of 50/50. `up` therefore also destabilizes pod-level fairness inside one QoS parent.
- `quota`: the limited group stays at 26.1-26.4% across modes, so `cpu.max` enforcement is independent of cgroup_mode.
- `quota`: the limited group is throttled in 81-100% of CFS periods; the CPU cap itself is the same in every mode. `up` is the outlier at 81% because its group does not always exhaust the quota in a period.
- `latency`: `up` p99 wakeup delay is 1327 us.
- `latency`: `smp` p99 wakeup delay is 697 us.
- `latency`: `concur` p99 wakeup delay is 708 us.
- `latency`: `max` p99 wakeup delay is 876 us.
- `latency`: `tasks` p99 wakeup delay is 1219 us.
- `latency`: the best p99.9 tail is `max` (2512 us, max 4263 us); the worst is `up` (4381 us, max 7257 us). The 1 ms probe is a tail-latency check, not a throughput metric.
- `up` vs `smp`: the measured group ratios range 0.52x-1.46x. The idealized model gives them the same share; the difference is the per-CPU placement effect that `up` keeps at full group weight.
- Context switches on `weighted_threads` range 2972/s (`max`) to 3349/s (`up`); the extra thread scaling in `concur`/`tasks`/`up` costs preemptions, while `smp`/`max` stay lower.
